value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The business the person had an interest in, keyed the way the business is keyed in BLADE. The later business owner tables replaced the truncated ABN hash, which runs through to 2021-22, with this identifier; the 2023-24 data item list calls it the BLADE number. Because BLADE holds business activity statements, business income tax filings, PAYG and Single Touch Payroll for "all active businesses from 2001-02 to current", the key is what lets a partner or sole trader be joined to their business's turnover, employment and survival. The person on the same row is identified by the synthetic person key instead.
value_definition: An opaque business-level identifier, one value per business unit, stable across BLADE tables and across the business owner tables that carry it.
limitation: A business identifier is not a business as an owner would describe it: a restructure or a new ABN can mint a new key for the same underlying operation, so ownership spells break where the entity is reorganised. The key also carries no industry, size or location, all of which have to come from the BLADE frame.
rationale: The 2023-24 business owner tables label the field 'BLADE number' while the earlier tables in the same series use a hashed ABN in the same position, and ABS publishes what BLADE is and which business data it combines. The switch from hashed ABN to BLADE number is read from the data item list rather than from a published note.
evidence_quote: The current BLADE asset contains data on all active businesses from 2001-02 to current
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried no description at all from the custodian and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page named a column with nothing behind it.

value_domain: Income year the ownership record belongs to
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return and instructions 2024
variable_description: The income year in which the person is recorded as owning the business, running 1 July to 30 June. Each table covers one year and each row is a person-business pair within it, so a spell of ownership is reconstructed by stacking years rather than by reading a start and end date. The underlying record comes from the annual return the business lodges, and the ATO does not require a partnership return where the only joint income was "rent from a jointly owned investment property", interest from a joint account or dividends from jointly held shares, so passive co-ownership does not generate a row.
value_definition: A financial year label for the table the row sits in, constant within a table and used to order the yearly files into a panel.
limitation: It dates the return, not the ownership. A partnership formed in March and one formed the previous July look identical, and a business that ceased mid-year still appears for the whole year, so entry and exit cannot be dated more finely than annually. Some tables also come in twelve-month and sixteen-month extract versions for the same year, which are different vintages of the same reporting year rather than different periods.
rationale: The business owner tables are built one file per income year from the annual partnership and sole trader returns, and the ATO instructions for that return state who must lodge it, which sets the population the yearly file covers. The mapping from the field to the return's income year is read from the table structure rather than from a published data dictionary.
evidence_quote: You don't need to lodge a partnership tax return if you were not in a partnership carrying on a business or where the only income you derived jointly (or in common) with another person was: rent from a jointly owned investment property
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Financial year' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that the year dates the return rather than the ownership, or that the sixteen-month tables are a second vintage of the same year.

variable_description: The individual whose interest in a business the row records, as the key that carries them across the whole asset. Each row pairs one person with one business for one year, so the rows under a key are that person's ownership history: how many businesses, over how many years, and as a partner or a sole trader according to which table the row sits in. Because the key is the PLIDA spine identifier, that history joins to the same person's wage income, Centrelink payments and Census answers, which is what makes questions about who starts a business answerable. In this package the values are synthetic and stand for nobody.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, one value per person, stable across the yearly partnership and sole trader tables and across every other dataset linked through the Spine.
limitation: It records a link to a business, not control of one: a silent partner and a working partner look identical, and the row carries no ownership share. Company directors and shareholders are outside these tables entirely, so a person running an incorporated business has no row here at all.
rationale: The data item list gives the field as the synthetic person identifier on every business owner table, and ABS publishes what the Spine is, which datasets build it and why each dataset is linked to it once, which is what determines what this key can be joined to.
evidence_quote: Instead of linking datasets one-to-one for individual projects, we can link all datasets to the Spine once and then combine datasets via the Spine as needed for multiple projects.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what a row means or that incorporated businesses are out of scope.
